post.description: Emitted from a harvester CALIBRATION reading, throttled to one event per screen per `windowSeconds` (the payload is the average over that window). Each channel is scored against the screen's latest calibration baseline. When the screen is not calibrated, channel references are null and status is `UNKNOWN`. The `black` channel is not scored (no calibration baseline exists for it).

Emitted once when a harvester completes (re)calibration for its screen and a fresh calibration baseline baseline takes effect — the discrete companion to the continuous `screen.quality` drift signal. `baseline` carries the new per-channel reference (same units as `screen.quality` `reference`). `recalibration` is `true` when the screen already had a baseline, meaning references on earlier `screen.quality` events are superseded. `calibratedAt` matches the `calibratedAt` that subsequent `screen.quality` events will report.

Emitted when Vojo hears from a Harvester and records its last check-in, at most once per Harvester every 5 minutes, so a Harvester that stays online sends one event about every 5 minutes. Treat a Harvester as offline when you have had no event for it for longer than that (for example 15 minutes). The time is when Vojo received the data, not the device's own clock, so it never moves backwards when a Harvester that was offline catches up on old readings. Scoped like the screen events: an endpoint limited to some screens or sites hears only Harvesters on those screens or sites, and a Harvester that is not on a screen reaches only endpoints that cover the whole organisation. Existing endpoints must subscribe to it explicitly. To read the same state on demand, use `GET /v1/harvesters`.

Emitted when a wrapper that `POST /v1/wrappers` accepted with `202` finishes building. `data` is the v1 `Wrapper` resource (status `ready`), identical to `GET /v1/wrappers/{wrapper_id}`. Not emitted for wrappers returned ready with `201`.
Emitted when a wrapper accepted with `202` fails to build. `data` is the v1 `Wrapper` resource with status `failed` and `failure` set.
Emitted when a harvester reading is verified against a known creative (proof of play). Now also carries a `freeze` block — the play's freeze quality on the `6 -> 12` bar scale.

post.summary: Passport (WRAPPER) lifecycle ping — start and end both observed
post.description:
verification.ping (Passport/WRAPPER, this one), verification.pod (Harvester/PoD), verification.pop (Player/PoP — not yet available, no Player-matching exists today), and the trust score: verification.score.preliminary (real time) then verification.score.final (settled; `verification.score` is its deprecated alias).

Emitted once a play's Passport track has recorded BOTH a start (`CONTENT_STARTED`) and an end (`CONTENT_FINISHED`) event — not on first evidence. `events` carries the full raw event data for the play's Passport track, not a derived status — a play that only ever records `CONTENT_STARTED` (abandoned, never finishes) correctly never fires this event. Settle-once per `(endpoint, playId, eventType)` — an endpoint subscribed to both this and `verification.score.final` receives one of each per play.

post.summary: Harvester (PoD) reading matched to a play
post.description:
Proof of Display: emitted the first time a Harvester reading is matched to a play, i.e. an optical sensor on the screen saw the creative's fingerprint. Unlike `verification.ping` there is no lifecycle to wait out — the first matched reading is the whole signal, so this fires at most once per `(endpoint, play)`, as soon as the reading is matched. A play can later receive further readings; they do not fire again. An endpoint subscribed after a play's first reading may receive that play's event when a later reading arrives. A reading can reach a play after its score became final, so this can follow `verification.score.final`, and the score doesn't include that reading. `events` carries the play's Harvester readings at firing time (usually exactly one). Settle-once per `(endpoint, playId, eventType)`.

`createdAt` on each reading is the device-reported time. On v1 Harvester firmware it is floored to a 10-minute bucket, so use the play's `t0` — not `createdAt` — to place the play in time. The freeze, jitter, offset and detect measurements are not yet reported by the Harvester pipeline and are therefore not part of this payload.

post.summary: Preliminary score — a play's score as soon as its Passport report completes
post.description:
The play's trust score as it stands when its Passport track has recorded both a start and a finish — the same moment `verification.ping` fires — so a score is available in real time, before the play settles. It can still change, up or down: evidence that arrives before the play settles (a Harvester read, or one that contradicts Passport) is scored, and `verification.score.final` then reports the settled score, which may be higher or lower. Use this one for live views; bill or report on the final one.

Fires at most once per `(endpoint, playId)`; a rescore before the play settles does not fire again. Not sent for a play that has already settled by the time its Passport report completes (its `verification.score.final` is the event to use), nor for a play with no Passport report (Harvester-only plays get only the final event). Not filtered by a filter policy: any endpoint subscribed to it receives it for plays in its scope.

The same event as `verification.score.final`, with the same payload, under its old name. Existing subscriptions keep receiving it unchanged. New integrations subscribe to `verification.score.final` (and `verification.score.preliminary` for a real-time score). An endpoint subscribed to both names receives one event per play, `verification.score.final`, and moving an endpoint from this name to the new one does not resend plays it has already received.

post.summary: Final score — a play reached FINAL and passed the endpoint's filter policy
post.description:
Emitted once a play reaches `FINAL` and clears the endpoint's filter policy. Settle-once per `(endpoint, playId, eventType)` — a play is reported to a given endpoint at most once, ever, even across retries or a later rescore. Only plays that reach FINAL at or after the filter policy's creation are reported.

Public API (/v1) subscribers: subscribing an endpoint to `verification.score.final` (or the `verification.score` alias) through `POST /v1/webhook-endpoints` (or adding it with `PATCH /v1/webhook-endpoints/{id}`) automatically gives that endpoint a permissive filter policy: no minimum band, no event minimums and no backfill. The event therefore fires for every play in the endpoint's scope that reaches FINAL after the subscription is made, and never replays past plays. `attestConfigId` in the payload is the id of that filter policy. An endpoint that already has a filter policy keeps it unchanged. Filters are not configurable through /v1 yet (planned as an additive change).

QualityStatus.description: GOOD within +/- the org quality threshold of 100; UNKNOWN when not assessable.

QualityChannel.description: One scored channel. `score = round(value / reference * 100)`; 100 = on the calibrated baseline.

value.description: The measured reading (averaged over the window).

reference.description: The calibration baseline this channel was scored against. Null when uncalibrated.

score.description: round(value / reference * 100). Null when not computable.

Freeze.description: Freeze quality, symmetric about the ideal sample count 6. `score = 100 - (abs(value-6)/(12-6))*100`, clamped 0..100 (6 -> 100; 0 and 12 -> 0; 3 and 9 -> 50).

score.description: 0..100; 100 = ideal (value == low anchor 6), falling to 0 as value deviates by the span (0 at value 0 or 12).

windowSeconds.description: The throttle/averaging window this payload covers.

windowEndAt.description: Epoch (seconds) of the latest reading in this window. Use for staleness — absence of events means no data, not "healthy".

thresholdPct.description: GOOD/BAD band half-width around 100 (org qualityThreshhold, default 10 = +/-10%). Symmetric, so both over-bright and too-dim are BAD. Same value for brightness and every colour channel. null when no alerting config.
